role: The second reading: each entry read to refute it, not to admire it.
method: Each fragment read whole beside what show.cjs prints for the grape (GRAPES, GRAPES_PLUS, TASTE, INTRO_GRAPES, GRID_SAY, GRID_READS, the service rows) and beside the Codex's region records, banks, producers file and service reference where they name the grape or a place the entry leans on.

Every fact the reviewed records do not already state was put to search: the appellation rules (Côte-Rôtie, Châteauneuf-du-Pape, Saint-Péray, Bellet, Vermentino di Gallura, Rivesaltes, the Terra Alta mark, the Alsace sweetness wording), the histories (the Victorian vines, the California Roussanne that was Viognier, the cuttings of 1992, the end of the name Tokay), the synonyms, and the notes of the glass where nothing in the Codex stood behind one.

The glass read as a blind taster would: each note asked whether a taster would nod, each prose field scanned by a script for a family word in disguise, each ladder set beside the Codex's own climate line for the region and beside the other five ladders of the chunk.

Each side by side read for a lazy generalisation, each blur for the exception it leaves out, each call put to a flight that holds the awkward bottle (a Chignin-Bergeron beside a Paso Robles Roussanne, an Eden Valley Viognier beside a Condrieu, a Terra Alta wine beside a Californian one).

The four lines counted and said aloud for the five beats in order; the sale read for its two sentences; the cards and questions read for one key, four options of one kind, a stem that gives nothing away and no question asked in the negative; the compare tells read from both sides against every fragment written so far that names these grapes.

node .scripts/grapes/build-grapes.cjs --lint --chunk g3 run after every round of edits until it printed six of six sound. The writing build was never run and no file but the six fragments and this record was touched.
limits: This session reached search alone: no source address could be opened (www.vins-rhone.com and www.wineaustralia.com did not resolve from here, and no further host was tried). A page is cited as search results quoted it, and every address the authors gave stays unconfirmed.

The brief allows five searches a grape. Viognier took four, Marsanne five, Roussanne four, Grenache Blanc five and Vermentino five; Pinot Gris took six, one over, the sixth to read the New Zealand growers' own page on style.
Where a source's address names a producer or a living person it is left out and the source is cited by its title alone.
Albariño and Macabeo are not yet written, so the Vermentino and Grenache Blanc tells against them were read from one side only.

codexRecords: js/reference.js, the Viognier and Gewürztraminer profiles: Viognier's other notes read musk and ginger, while Gewürztraminer's confuse line says Viognier is apricot and honeysuckle without the lychee or spice. The two reviewed records pull apart. The table sides with the second (ginger is Gewürztraminer's lead note there); the owner may want ginger out of the Viognier profile, or the confuse line softened.

js/data-intro.js, the Roussanne row: its wines read Hermitage, Châteauneuf-du-Pape blanc (with Marsanne). Marsanne is not among the grapes Châteauneuf-du-Pape permits. The author's flag, confirmed on every list read; the row is the Régionale course's own and is left alone.

js/data-intro.js, the Régionale rows: Vermentino's reviewed profile opens its fruit on the bare word Citrus, and Roussanne's row says herbal tea and white flowers. Family words, as the author says; the table names the things.
The Codex's Rhône bank says Roussanne ripens late; the Rhône body is quoted as early to mid. Not tested further, since the entry states neither.

The Codex's producers file records Ermitage as one house's spelling of Hermitage, and its Swiss record gives Ermitage as Marsanne in the Valais. Both are right; the Marsanne label row now carries both, so the two records no longer trip a reader.
unsettled: Vermentino on French labels. Three trade reports of 2022 say an annex of the European labelling regulation keeps the grape name for Italy, Australia, the United States and Croatia, and that French growers were told to stop using it from the 2022 harvest. Two searches found no later change and no later confirmation. The half line is struck; restore it only on a current source.

The year Grenache Blanc was approved as a name for American labels. The author gives 2002 on two growers' bodies; a search confirmed varietal bottles since 2002 and no date of approval. The card now says about ten years after 1992.

The Gewürztraminer entry of chunk g2 says in its Viognier tell that Viognier has no lychee or ginger. It is another chunk's fragment and was not touched; with ginger now out of the Viognier notes the two entries agree, and only the reviewed Viognier profile still prints ginger.

Whether Virginia Viognier is, as a style, fresher than California's. Nothing read says so and the Codex reads Virginia's summers as hot and humid, so the claim is out; a regional source could put it back.
A second citrus note for Marsanne, and nectarine for Vermentino: neither confirmed.
Whether every source address still answers: none could be opened from this session.
settled: Côte-Rôtie: the Viognier is fermented with the Syrah, not blended in afterwards; two sources agree, so never blended in afterwards stands on the third Viognier card.
Roussanne's side by side: varietal Roussanne from Washington's Columbia Valley is on sale under several labels, so the plan's mode stands.
Vermentino di Gallura: DOCG by the decree of 11 September 1996 and at least 95 per cent Vermentino.
Alsace: the sweetness wording is compulsory from the 2021 vintage, so the guest answer that sends a guest to the word sec stands.
